It continues the narrative from folio 104 (Epaminondas restores Messenia; Thessalian cities ask Thebes for help against the tyrant Alexander of Pherae) and runs on into folio 106.

Content in order:
(1) An army is sent under Pelopidas, who defeats Alexander, besieges Larissa and forces its surrender.
(2) After settling affairs, Pelopidas goes to Macedonia, then troubled by a succession dispute. He brings the young Philip (later Philip II) to Thebes as a hostage.
(3) In '367' he is sent again to Thessaly as an envoy. Alexander seizes him and throws him into prison, so the Thebans send a second army.
(4) Epaminondas' political opponents have kept him from the command, but he marches along as a common soldier.
(5) The army is surrounded by Alexander. The sentence continues on the next page: the soldiers acclaim Epaminondas general, and he frees the army and Pelopidas.

Historical dating is slightly compressed compared with modern chronology. Pelopidas' first Thessalian expedition and the taking of Philip as hostage are usually placed c. 369/368 BC. His capture by Alexander of Pherae is usually placed in 368 BC, and his rescue by Epaminondas in 367 BC. The notebook's '367' for the embassy and arrest is about a year late by common reckonings, but this is within the range of 19th-century textbook chronologies.
